related_questions.question: What are the new requirements for travel to the UK?

text_blocks.snippet: For US citizens traveling to the UK starting January 8, 2025, an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) is required for entry or transit through the UK. This requirement applies to those not needing a visa for short stays, including tourism, business, or family visits. The ETA is digitally linked to your passport and is valid for two years. You can apply online through the UK ETA website or the UK ETA mobile app.
snippet_highlighted_words: an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) is required for entry or transit through the UK

list.snippet: Who needs it: US citizens traveling to the UK for visits of up to six months, including transit through UK airports, who do not already have a UK visa.
Validity: Two years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first.
How to apply: Apply online through the UK ETA website or mobile app.
Important Note: Travelers without an approved ETA will be denied boarding.
Passport Validity: Your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay.
Transit through UK Airports: If transiting without passing through border control, an ETA may not be required.

text_blocks.snippet: In essence, if you are a US citizen planning a trip to the UK starting January 8, 2025, you will need to apply for an ETA before traveling. This applies even if you are just passing through a UK airport (transiting).

related_questions.question: Is it safe to travel to England right now from the USA?

text_blocks.snippet: It is generally safe to travel to England from the USA, but travelers should be aware of potential risks and exercise caution. The UK faces a threat of terrorism, with the government assessing an attack as likely. There is also a risk of violent crimes like muggings and knife crime, as well as petty theft like pickpocketing.
snippet_highlighted_words: It is generally safe to travel to England from the USA, but travelers should be aware of potential risks and exercise caution

list.title: Terrorism:
list.snippet: The UK has a "substantial" threat level for terrorism, meaning an attack is considered likely. Travelers should be alert, monitor media for updates, and follow instructions from local authorities.

list.title: Violent Crime:
list.snippet: While violent crime rates are lower than in many US cities, petty theft like pickpocketing and bag snatching are common, particularly in crowded tourist areas.

list.title: Petty Theft:
list.snippet: Be aware of your surroundings and take precautions to protect your belongings, especially on public transport and in busy areas.

list.title: Monitor Official Sources:
list.snippet: Check the U.S. Department of State's website and the UK government's travel advice for the latest updates and advisories.

list.title: Enroll in STEP:
list.snippet: Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to receive alerts and allow the embassy to contact you in case of an emergency.

list.title: Be Alert:
list.snippet: Stay aware of your surroundings, particularly in crowded tourist locations and on public transport.

list.title: Follow Local Advice:
list.snippet: Pay attention to any instructions or warnings issued by local authorities.

list.title: Prepare for Demonstrations:
list.snippet: Be aware that demonstrations or protests can occur in the UK, especially in London. Check local media for updates and adjust your plans accordingly.

list.title: COVID-19:
list.snippet: There are currently no COVID-19 restrictions in place for travelers entering England.

text_blocks.snippet: In summary: While the UK is generally safe, it's crucial to be aware of potential risks like terrorism and petty theft and to take necessary precautions while traveling. By staying informed and exercising caution, you can have a safe and enjoyable trip.
